600H: Evac+Chair Dual-Position Wheelchair Evacuation Chair
Product URL: https://www.anchortex.com/products/evac-chair-600h-evacuation-stair-chair
Manufacturer page: https://www.evac-chair.com/evacuation-chairs/evacchair-600h/
Spec sheet: 600H data sheet
Keywords (Ricky's sheet): Primary: evacuation wheelchair (80/mo, KD8). Secondary: wheelchair evacuation chair (20), evac chair 600h (10). Ricky's note: dual-position model per the product copy; KD8 is the highest in this set. Andrew's note (Tab 1): we do not sell an evacuation wheelchair, so the term is used to explain what the chair does instead.
Recommended H1 and Subtitle
H1: Evac+Chair Dual-Position Wheelchair Evacuation Chair with Carry Handles – 600H
Current H1: Evac+Chair 600H Evacuation Stair Chair
Subtitle: Flat or Hammock Seat and Fold-Away Carry Handles for Downward and Upward Evacuation, Used in Place of an Evacuation Wheelchair on Stairs
Current subtitle: Evac+Chair 600H Stairway Evacuation Chair
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Evac+Chair 600H is a dual-position wheelchair evacuation chair that lets one operator move a person with limited mobility safely down the stairs in an emergency. It is used in place of an evacuation wheelchair on stairs, where a standard wheelchair cannot go, and its seat switches between a flat seat and a hammock seat to suit the passenger.
Self-braking Evac+Track friction tracks control the speed of descent, and fold-away front and rear grab handles let 2 to 4 people lift the chair for upward evacuation, such as from a basement, or through locations with difficult access. At 24 lbs, the 600H folds for wall mounted storage and is ready to use in seconds.
Operation: One operator for descent; fold-away front and rear grab handles let 2 to 4 people lift the chair for upward evacuation
Dual Position Seat: Flat seat with zipped side panels, or release the panels and fasten them underneath for a hammock seat, chosen each time
Tracks: Self-braking, reinforced Evac+Track friction tracks control the speed of descent
Head Restraint: Adjustable patient head restraint limits movement and secures the passenger
Safety Belts: Quick-release head, chest, and thigh belts, with an over-thigh restraint in both seat positions
Handle: Ergonomic adjustable handle for easy deployment and compact storage
Wheels: Heavy duty wheels for uneven ground, with lockable rear wheels to keep the chair stationary
Visibility: Reflective decals for poor visibility
Weight Capacity: 400 lbs
Weight: 24 lbs
Storage: Folds for compact storage and is wall mountable
Certifications: FDA registered
Compliance: Exceeds fire safety requirements and emergency response guidelines established to support the Americans with Disabilities Act
Includes: 3 passenger safety belts (head, chest, thigh), photoluminescent signage, wall mounting brackets, dust cover, and user guide
Warranty: Lifetime manufacturer’s warranty
Design: Designed in the United States
Available Models and Options
600H – Dual-Position Evacuation Chair: Flat or hammock seat, carry handles for upward evacuation, 400 lb capacity
[H2] Applications
The 600H suits buildings where people with limited mobility may need to be moved down, or up, the stairs in an emergency.
Typical applications include:
Hospitals, nursing homes, and care facilities
Buildings with basements or lower floors, where people must be evacuated up the stairs
Locations with difficult access, such as tight stairwells and small landings
Offices, schools, hotels, and high-rise buildings, when the elevators cannot be used
Explore Anchortex's Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection for more evacuation equipment.
[H2] Frequently Asked Questions
Is the Evac+Chair 600H an evacuation wheelchair?
It does the job of an evacuation wheelchair on the stairs. It is a folding evacuation chair, not an everyday wheelchair: the passenger moves into the chair, and the operator guides it down the stairs on its tracks.
Can the 600H go up the stairs?
Yes, with help. One operator takes the 600H down the stairs. For upward evacuation, 2 to 4 people use the fold-away front and rear grab handles to lift the chair up the stairs.
What is the dual-position seat?
The seat can be used flat, with zipped side panels, or as a hammock seat by releasing the side panels and fastening them underneath. The over-thigh quick-release restraint works in both positions.
How is the 600H different from the 300H?
The 600H adds fold-away front and rear grab handles, so 2 to 4 people can carry it up the stairs or through difficult access. The 300H is the lighter standard model for downward evacuation.
[H2] About Evac+Chair Evacuation Chairs
Evac+Chair makes stair evacuation chairs, powered stair chairs, evacuation sleds, and accessories for moving people with limited mobility on stairs, in an emergency or every day.
The Evac+Chair line includes:
Emergency evacuation chairs: The 300H, 400H, 600H, and 750H stair evacuation chairs for controlled travel down the stairs
Powered stair climbing chairs: The battery powered Power 800 and Power 900 for going up and down the stairs
Stair transport seat: The IBEX 700H Tran-Seat for two-person transport up and down the stairs
Evacuation sleds and mats: The Evac+Sled, Ulti-Mat, and Evac+Sheet rescue sheet
Accessories: Comfy Seat, transfer seat, storage cabinets, anti-theft alarms, and the iEvac smoke and fire escape hood
[H2] About Evac+Chair
Evac+Chair has made stairway evacuation chairs since 1982, and its chairs were designed in the United States. Explore the full line of Evac+Chair evacuation chairs at Anchortex.

Notes and Questions
Keywords and your note: you said we do not sell an evacuation wheelchair, and Ricky's primary keyword for this page is "evacuation wheelchair" (80/mo). The search results for it are evacuation chair pages (Stryker evacuation chairs, and stores selling this 600H, which Evac+Chair itself calls a "dual-position evacuation wheelchair"). So I used it the way you suggested: "used in place of an evacuation wheelchair on stairs" (subtitle and intro) and the FAQ "Is the Evac+Chair 600H an evacuation wheelchair?", which says it is not an everyday wheelchair. The H1, meta title, and meta description use the secondary keyword "wheelchair evacuation chair" (an evacuation chair for wheelchair users). Is this OK?
"Evacuation stair chair" is the 300H page's primary keyword, and "stair evacuation chair" / "emergency evacuation chair" stay on the collection page (Ricky), so I did not use them as main terms here.
FOLDED SIZE: the 600H data sheet and the Evac+Chair web page say 41"H x 20"W x 8"D, but those are the same numbers the Evac+Chair range brochure gives for the 300H. The brochure gives the 600H as 47"H x 23"W x 12"D, which matches our page. I left the folded size out until you confirm. 47 x 23 x 12 looks right, since the 600H has extra handles.
Upward evacuation: our page says "two operators are required to lift the chair"; the data sheet says "2 to 4 person upwards evacuation." I used 2 to 4 people.
Left out: "the only evacuation chair on the market with a dual position seat" (the brochure also lists a dual position seat on the 300H), "World's No.1," and "Successful in saving lives in 9/11."
Instructional DVD: on our page and the data sheet, but not on the Evac+Chair web page. I left it out of Includes. Is a DVD still included?
Duplicate content: our current description is the Evac+Chair text word for word (with a typo, "sage emergency evacuation"). The new copy is fully rewritten.
Images: images 2 and 3 are named "Evac_Chair300HEvacuationStairChair-FlatSeat" and "-HammockSeat." Are these 300H photos? Would you like me to replace or add 600H photos from the Evac+Chair website?
Shipping weight: the variant is set to 200 lbs. The chair weighs 24 lbs. Is 200 lbs the boxed weight?
Price: $2,150 with compare-at $2,867 (75%, not 80%). No change made.
Current meta description is a general GSA pricing line. Is GSA pricing still offered?
